title: Token-density-aware batch orchestrator with elastic slot consolidation
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context and motivation: production inference workloads show wide variation in token density (short prompts with long completions vs long prompts with short completions). Existing seqlen bucketing reduces padding but fails to consider token-density skew inside a slot and how KV cache hits change effective cost per request. This PR introduces a token-density-aware orchestrator that (1) estimates per-request token-cost density at enqueue time, (2) consolidates "elastic slots" by greedily coalescing high-density with low-density requests to balance GPU occupancy, and (3) applies a small kernel-alignment hint when forming device batches so quantized kernels avoid pathological padding overhead. Goals: reduce padded tokens across the workload, lower p95 latency variance during mixed workloads, and keep throughput stable without SLO violations. Design summary: - Token density score: a heuristic combining prompt_len / (prompt_len + expected_completion_len) with model-specific kernel-cost coefficients learned from runtime telemetry. The score is computed on request arrival and stored as a short-lived annotation for batching decisions. - Elastic slot consolidation: rather than fixed seqlen buckets, we create slots with a target token-budget. New requests are placed into existing slots where adding them increases expected utilization but keeps padding cost under a threshold; otherwise we open a new slot. Slots have a soft timeout to avoid head-of-queue starvation. - KV-aware dispatch: requests tagged with high KV-hit probabilities are preferentially grouped to the same slot when kernel alignment hints indicate contiguous KV cache layout to reduce cache thrash. - Kernel alignment hints: small metadata (~1 byte) attached to slot composition to request specific CUDA kernel shapes or quantization-friendly paths. Implementation highlights: - runtime/batcher/elastic_slot_batcher.{cc,hh}: new orchestrator implementation with slot bookkeeping and token-density scoring. - runtime/scheduler/kv_aware_dispatcher.{cc,hh}: compact dispatcher that uses KV hit probability to bias slot assignment. - runtime/metrics: added token_density_histogram and slot_utilization_ratio metrics and dashboard panels. - config: new flags in rconfig: batch.slot_target_tokens, batch.max_slot_pad_ratio, batch.elastic_timeout_ms. - migration: existing seqlen bucketing remains available and is the default; the new orchestrator is behind rconfig flag batch.strategy=elastic_token_density for controlled rollout. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for token-density scoring and slot consolidation logic - [x] Integration test with synthetic mixed workload generator - [x] Canary run on perf-canary with 72h windows - [x] Dashboard panels and alerts for slot starvation & padding regression Compatibility & safety: default behavior unchanged (seqlen bucketer remains default). The orchestrator is opt-in via rconfig and feature flag; metrics gated for first-stage rollout. Benchmarks (perf-canary synthetic workload that mixes 20% long prompts/short completions, 80% short prompts/long completions): - end-to-end token cost reduction: 18% median vs default seqlen-bucketed batching - p95 latency: improved by 12% on average across runs - tail variance: 25% lower measured as sigma(p95) across machines Observability & CI: added deterministic unit tests; CI pipeline shows full runtime build + integration_e2e suite passing. The canary run revealed an early KV-cache hotpath contention which was fixed by changing map iteration order in kv_aware_dispatcher and re-running canary. Review conversation (high level): - Marco Ruiz: requested clearer invariants around slot timeout and starvation; asked for an automated test that simulates prolonged high-density bursts. - Author (Aisha): added integration test burst_simulator.py and tuned soft timeout from 80ms->120ms after discussion. - Leah Chen: asked for explicit fallback when kernel alignment hint is unsupported; author added fallback to default kernel path and test coverage. - Omar Siddiq: approved after confirming telemetry and dashboards show no regression on memory usage. CI summary: initial run had one flaky test (kv_cache_eviction_test) failing on macOS runners; flaky test was stabilized by reducing time sensitivity and rerun passed. Merge notes: squash-merged to main after canary gating completed and perf metrics validated. Files touched (high level): - runtime/batcher/elastic_slot_batcher.cc - runtime/batcher/elastic_slot_batcher.hh - runtime/scheduler/kv_aware_dispatcher.cc - runtime/scheduler/kv_aware_dispatcher.hh - runtime/metrics/token_density_metrics.cc - runtime/config/rconfig_defaults.yaml - tests/batcher/test_elastic_slots.py - tests/integration/burst_simulator.py - docs/rfcs/2026-02-token-density-batching.md - dashboards/perf/token_density_orchestrator.json - examples/quickstarts/elastic-token-density.yaml How to try locally: set rconfig.batch.strategy=elastic_token_density and rconfig.batch.slot_target_tokens=4096; run bazel test //tests/..., start local runtime with --enable-experimental-batcher. Release notes: Introduces opt-in token-density-aware batch orchestrator with elastic slot consolidation, KV-aware dispatch, and kernel-alignment hints. Expected benefits: lower padded tokens and improved p95 latency for mixed-density workloads; no change to default behavior. Related: ENG-17834 (design), ENG-17902 (telemetry integration), SUP-6342 (customer report motivating KV-aware grouping).
